Saving this. Is it possible to start brewing with limited equipment and have drinkable beer to show for it?

Yes, the key things to a decent tasting beer are having clean equipment throughout the process and a stable temperature for your yeast to ferment at. If you don't have an ability to regulate the temperature (google fermentation chamber) then brew in accordance with the seasons like they used to.

If you start with extract kits all you need to a pot and a fermenting bucket/carboy, plus some bottles for after it has fermented.

That recipe is an all grain one, so it requires a bit more equipment, but you should be able to find malt extract that you can boil up, rather than mashing the grain. Using extract skips the whole mashing business and is easier, so it is perfect for beginners.
